info.name: Authentication - OAuth V2
info.description:
This Postman collection validates OAuth 2.0 authentication flows for **Retail** and **Business** users. It supports two authentication approaches: **Access Token–based flows** and **OIDC**.

Access Token Flows

**• Client Credentials** – Institution-level access for server-to-server communication

**• Password Grant** – User-level access using login credentials

item.name: 🔗 Client Credential

request.description:
Retrieve the list of accounts for the authenticated user.

```
GET /v1/accounts?hostUserId={{retail_user_host_user_id}}
```

Revoke the current access token so it can no longer authorize API requests.

```
DELETE /oauth2/v1/revoke
```

Call a protected endpoint with the revoked token to confirm it is no longer valid.

```
GET /v1/accounts?hostUserId={{retail_user_host_user_id}}
```

item.description:
## 🔄 Retail User – Client Credentials Flow

| **Step** | Request Name | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Generate Access Token | Obtain an access token using client credentials. |
| 2 | Get List of Accounts | Access a protected resource using the access token. |
| 3 | Revoke Access Token | Invalidate the access token to prevent further use. |
| 4 | Verify Token Revocation | Confirm that the revoked token no longer grants access. |

item.name: 🔗 Password

request.description:
Retrieve the list of accounts for the authenticated user.

```
GET /v1/accounts
```

Exchange a refresh token for a new access token.

Saves `access_token_refresh` to the environment.

```
POST /oauth2/v1/token
```

Call a protected endpoint with the refreshed access token to confirm it is valid.

```
GET /v1/accounts
```

Revoke the refreshed access token so it can no longer authorize API requests.

```
DELETE /oauth2/v1/revoke
```

Call a protected endpoint with the revoked token to confirm it is no longer valid.

```

item.description:
## 🔄 Retail User – Password Flow

| **Step** | Request Name | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Generate Access Token | Obtain access and refresh tokens using the user's credentials. |
| 2 | Get List of Accounts | Access a protected resource using the access token. |
| 3 | Generate Refresh Token | Use the refresh token to obtain a new access token. |
| 4 | Verify Refreshed Token | Validate the new access token obtained via refresh. |
| 5 | Revoke Access Token | Invalidate the access token to prevent further use. |
| 6 | Verify Token Revocation | Confirm that the revoked token no longer grants access. |

Authorize the client for the OIDC flow and obtain the scopes required to generate an authorization code.

Retrieve the list of accounts for the authenticated user.

```

Exchange a refresh token for a new access token.

Saves `access_token_refresh` to the environment.

```
POST /oauth2/v1/token
```

Call a protected endpoint with the refreshed access token to confirm it is valid.

```
GET /v1/accounts
```

Revoke the refreshed access token so it can no longer authorize API requests.

```
DELETE /oauth2/v1/revoke
```

Call a protected endpoint with the revoked token to confirm it is no longer valid.

```
GET /v1/accounts
```

item.description:
## 🔄 Retail User – OIDC Flow

| **Step** | Request Name | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Generate Access Token | Obtain an access token using client credentials. This represents a pre-authenticated retail user. |
| 2 | Search for Retail User Institution ID | (Optional) Use this step to locate the retail user institution ID if it’s not already available. |
| 3 | Client Authorization | Retrieve approved scopes and authorization policies for the partner OIDC client. |
| 4 | Generate Authorization Code | Issue a short-lived authorization code with API and OIDC scopes, simulating post-login user consent. |
| 5 | Exchange Code for Tokens | Exchange the code for an access token, ID token, and (if requested) a refresh token. |
| 6 | Get List of Accounts | Access a protected resource using the access token. |
| 7 | Generate Refresh Token | Use the refresh token to obtain a new access token. |
| 8 | Verify Refreshed Token | Validate the new access token obtained via refresh. |
| 9 | Revoke Access Token | Invalidate the access token to prevent further use. |
| 10 | Verify Token Revocation | Confirm that the revoked token no longer grants access. |

item.name: 🔗 Client Credential

request.description:
Retrieve the business customer record and identify `institution_customer_id` for subsequent requests.

Saves `institution_customer_id` to the environment.

```
GET /v1/customers/{{business_user_login_id}}?userIdType=LOGIN_ID
```

Retrieve the list of accounts for the authenticated user.

```
GET /v1/accounts?loginId={{business_user_login_id}}&institutionCustomerId={{institution_customer_id}}
```

Revoke the current access token so it can no longer authorize API requests.

```
DELETE /oauth2/v1/revoke
```

Call a protected endpoint with the revoked token to confirm it is no longer valid.

```
GET /v1/accounts?loginId={{business_user_login_id}}&institutionCustomerId={{institution_customer_id}}
```

item.description:
## 🔄 Business User – Client Credentials Flow

| **Step** | Request Name | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Generate Access Token | Obtain an access token using client credentials. |
| 2 | Search for Business Entity | (Optional) Use this step to locate the institution customer ID if it’s not already available. Retrieve business user details and match the memberNumber (TIN/EIN) to identify the corresponding institutionCustomerId. |
| 3 | Get List of Accounts | Access a protected resource using the access token. |
| 4 | Revoke Access Token | Invalidate the access token to prevent further use. |
| 5 | Verify Token Revocation | Confirm that the revoked token no longer grants access. |
